conviction_note: abs_move 10% (the 9.76% option-implied move, the name's recent large reactions of +19.3% and +10.6%, and a new CEO giving his first December-quarter guide) times p_up 55 gives +1.0. Mid-quarter statements, counterparty capex and peer bookings lean positive, and the stock is down 50% from its high and below the lowest analyst target. Against that, put skew is +19 vol points, peers ASMPT and Besi guide next-quarter revenue flat, and the last beat-and-raise was sold (-3.4%). impact_sum is +1.7, close to the scaled +1.0; it is larger because many small positive counterparty items add up, and some of them may already be priced.
bar: Fiscal Q4 2026 (Sep quarter) revenue $375m +/- $20m and non-GAAP EPS $1.42 +/- 10%: company guide in the Q3 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000056978/000005697826000030/ex991liveq32026.htm (2026-08-05). Street consensus is $1.44 EPS on $375m (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KLIC/23157); another aggregate quoted in search shows $1.46 EPS on $384.3m. The whisper is $1.61, above the top of the guide. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimates that roughly agree, so no cap applies. No December-quarter (Q1 FY27) street figure was found. The only forward figure is FY27 revenue of about $1.52B (stockanalysis, updated 2026-11-09), roughly 4x the Q4 guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 2.2m shares, 4.2% of shares outstanding, 3.7 days to cover at the latest settlement (sweep dates it 2026-11-13; the page gives no date). It fell about 96k shares (-4.2%) from the prior settlement and is marked 'falling' (https://equibles.com/stocks/klic/summary, read 2026-11-18). This is not a crowded short. The baseline shows 25-delta skew of +19.31 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest of 0.25 (call-heavy open interest), and front-expiry ATM IV of 151.6%. The ATM spread is 53% of mid, so the implied move and skew are indicative only.

expectations.price_path: 5-day -9.59% and 20-day -18.73% into the print (sealed baseline, spot $66.18 at 2026-11-18 18:13 UTC). The stock is 50.5% below its 52-week high and down 22% since the 2026-08-05 report (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11). Exact SOXX/SMH returns over the same 5 and 20 days were not found. The sector fell on 2026-11-05, when the PHLX SOX lost 12.25% in one session and SOXX about 23% that week (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/06/chip-stocks-just-had-their-second-worst-day-on-record/). KLIC's 20-day fall is therefore roughly in line with the sector, not an idiosyncratic underperformance.
expectations.vs_targets: Spot about $66 against a mean target of $95, median $100, high $115 (Needham Buy) and low $70 (B. Riley Hold, cut from $86 on 2026-11-09). Spot is below the lowest target (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/klic/forecast/, updated 2026-11-09).
expectations.whisper_or_buyside_bar: Whisper EPS $1.61 against $1.44 consensus and the $1.56 top of the guide. The preview says December-quarter guidance is the key test and a flat or down sequential outlook would conflict with management's first-half FY27 commentary (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KLIC/23157, 2026-11-11).
expectations.last_print: Fiscal Q3 2026 (reported 2026-08-05): non-GAAP EPS $1.20, beating by $0.14 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/kulicke-and-soffa-industries-nasdaqklic-issues-quarterly-earnings-results-beats-expectations-by-014-eps-2026-08-05/). Q4 revenue guide $375m against a $328.8m street figure, about 14% above (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/kulicke-and-soffa-industries-nasdaqklic-releases-q4-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-05/). The stock moved -3.39% (baseline). In Feb 2026 a guide 25% above the street moved it +19.27%.
expectations.short_interest_trend: Latest 2.2m shares / 4.2% / 3.7 days to cover, about 2.3m at the prior settlement (implied from a -95.9k change); falling (https://equibles.com/stocks/klic/summary). In April 2026: 1.18m shares, 2.28% of float, 1.8 days (MarketBeat snippet). Short interest roughly doubled since spring but is still modest.
expectations.real_bar: Q4 revenue at or above the $375m midpoint with gross margin near 48%, plus a December-quarter guide at least flat sequentially (about $375m or more) and a reaffirmed FY27 thermocompression target of $150-200m from the new CEO. After a 50% drawdown a flat guide probably clears; a sequential decline does not.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: not found (no December-quarter Q1 FY27 consensus found in any source)
next_guide.street_full_year: FY2027 revenue about $1.52B and non-GAAP EPS $5.90 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/klic/forecast/, updated 2026-11-09)
next_guide.company_current_guide: Q4 FY26 revenue $375m +/- $20m, non-GAAP EPS $1.42 +/- 10%, non-GAAP opex $87.5m +/- 2% (Q3 8-K, 2026-08-05). Advanced Solutions/TCB revenue above $100m in FY26 and $150-200m in FY27 (call). No full-year FY27 guide; management declined to give one.
next_guide.basis: On the August call, purchase orders extended into fiscal Q2 2027 and management expected above-average first-half FY27 demand. The CEO said on 2026-10-18 that demand was improving across markets. Points against a sequential raise: ASMPT guides its SEMI segment flat next quarter on longer lead times, Besi guides Q4 flat +/-5%, and a new CEO's first guide may be set conservatively. On balance, roughly flat to modestly up sequentially.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is 50.5% below its 52-week high, down 22% since the 2026-08-05 report and 18.7% over 20 days, and at $66 sits below every analyst target (mean $95, low $70 after B. Riley cut from $86 on 2026-11-09). The bar the market holds is lower than the consensus figures that set it in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a sell-down into the Feb 2026 print, a guide 25% above the street moved the stock +19.27%. After a run-up into Aug 2026, a 14% guide beat moved it -3.39% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is priced in the sense that it is the price. What is not priced is the asymmetry: if expectations were still high, spot would sit near the $95 mean target with calls bid, not below the lowest target with puts bid.
findings.independence: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/klic/forecast/ (targets and the B. Riley cut, 2026-11-09). The sealed baseline gives the run-up and 52-week distance.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter (DIGITIMES, 2026-09-04), K&S said AI demand is spreading into adjacent applications, lifting 2026 wire-bonding equipment orders and driving wire-bond shipments to a record high. This was said inside the September quarter being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 reported-quarter beat (EPS +$0.14) moved the stock -3.39% (baseline), so reported-quarter strength has not paid on its own recently.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits behind a paywall on a Taiwanese trade site and appears in no US preview. It lands inside the $355-395m guide range the market was already told to expect, so it mostly supports the top half of the range rather than a surprise.
findings.independence: Separate from the CEO's 2026-10-18 interview (different date and outlet). Points the same way.

findings.finding: New CEO Raj Talluri (in post since 2026-09-01) said in a SemiWiki interview of 2026-10-18 that demand is improving across general semiconductor, memory, automotive and industrial markets. This is the latest company statement before the print, made after the September quarter closed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises are what moved this stock: +19.27% in Feb 2026 on a guide 25% above the street, +10.6% in Nov 2025 (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell from about $92 (2026-10-09) to $66 after the interview, so the market took the sector selloff over this statement. If it were priced, the December guide risk would show in a narrower implied move or a smaller put skew.
findings.independence: Original interview: https://semiwiki.com/ceo-interviews/373948-ceo-interview-with-dr-raj-talluri-of-kulicke-soffa/ (2026-10-18). Same interview, counted once.

findings.finding: On the 2026-08-06 Q3 call, management said purchase orders extend into fiscal Q2 2027 (the March 2027 quarter), which it called unusual for the business. It also said traditional wire-bond capacity had been expanded about fourfold in two quarters and that first-half FY27 demand was above average. This supports a December-quarter guide at least flat against the $375m Q4 midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August guide beat (14% above the street) was sold at -3.39% after a run. The February guide beat (25% above) was bought at +19.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since August, but the stock has halved since the July high, with the sector, so the market is discounting how long the order book lasts. If the order book were trusted, the stock would not trade below the lowest target. Snippet only (the page returned 403).
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-11) repeats that purchase orders reach into mid-FY27. Same source chain, so not independent.

findings.finding: ASE, a top OSAT customer for bonders, raised its 2026 capex a third time on 2026-10-29, to US$11.5B from US$10.5B, and said 2027 capex will be higher still. Q3 equipment capex was US$2.1B, with US$1.0B for packaging.
findings.link: ASE is the largest OSAT and a long-standing buyer of K&S ball and wedge bonders. ASE's packaging equipment capex is the budget K&S bonders are sold into; K&S's share of ASE capex is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. KLIC fell after the ASE print with the sector.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but it has not been mapped to KLIC's December guide in any preview found. Much of ASE's raise goes to leading-edge packaging and test, not wire bond, so transmission is partial.

findings.finding: On its Q3 2026 call, Amkor narrowed its 2026 capex to about $2.5B (from $2.5-3.0B, on Arizona payment timing) and said capex will rise in 2027. Q3 revenue was $1.99B (+5% q/q), with record computing and automotive/industrial revenue, and the Q4 guide was $1.9-2.0B.
findings.link: Amkor is a top-3 OSAT and a buyer of wire bonders and advanced-packaging tools. The narrowing is construction timing, not equipment.
findings.why_not_priced: Mixed and public. The 2026 trim is construction, not tools, and 2027 is up. A small net positive.

findings.finding: Tianshui Huatian (16.9% of K&S revenue in 1H FY26) reported Q3 2026 revenue of RMB 6.26B (+36.1% y/y), on growth in packaging orders. Q3 net profit was RMB 287m, -9% y/y and about -60% q/q, which is margin pressure at K&S's largest customer.
findings.link: Huatian is K&S's largest single customer (16.9% of revenue per secondary reads of the FY26 10-Q). K&S's China-headquartered customers were about 57% of revenue in 1H FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: Chinese-language filing; no US preview maps Huatian volumes to the KLIC guide. Order growth supports bonder demand, but the profit squeeze could slow capex.

findings.finding: JCET, China's largest OSAT, reported record nine-month 2026 revenue of RMB 30.95B (+8%). Advanced-packaging revenue rose 54% y/y and capacity expansion continues (RMB 7.8B Lingang plant).
findings.link: JCET is a major Chinese OSAT and a wire-bond buyer. China-headquartered customers are about 57% of K&S revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Public, but not tied to KLIC in US coverage. Total revenue growth of 8% is modest, so the capacity read is mainly advanced packaging.
findings.independence: Separate from Huatian. Points the same way.

findings.finding: ASMPT, K&S's direct wire-bond and TCB competitor, reported record Q3 2026 group bookings of HK$8.85B (+138% y/y) on 2026-10-28, with all-time-high TCB bookings. Industry-wide back-end bonding demand is strong in the September quarter.
findings.link: Same products (wire bonders, TCB), the same OSAT and memory customers, and the same China channel. ASMPT SEMI revenue was US$374m, about the same size as K&S's quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Hong Kong-listed peer that reported after K&S last spoke. KLIC fell after it with the sector. Record TCB bookings at ASMPT may also be share taken from K&S, so the read-across is not clean.

findings.finding: Peers guide the December quarter flat. ASMPT says SEMI-segment revenue will be flat next quarter on longer advanced-packaging lead times (2026-10-28). Besi guides Q4 revenue flat +/-5% against Q3's EUR 283.4m. This argues against a sequential step-up in K&S's December-quarter guide.
findings.link: ASMPT SEMI is the closest like-for-like (wire bond plus TCB, same customers). Besi overlaps in die attach, TCB and hybrid bonding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises move KLIC most: +19.27% in Feb 2026 and -3.39% in Aug 2026 (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Peer guides abroad that are not mapped onto KLIC's December quarter. Street FY27 of $1.52B already implies a run rate near the Q4 guide, so a flat guide is roughly in line, and this is a risk to an upside guide rather than a miss.
findings.independence: https://quartr.com/events/be-semiconductor-industries-n-v-besi-q3-2026_3eFihym3 (Besi Q4 flat +/-5%). A different company, pointing the same way. Shares the ASMPT document with the ASMPT bookings finding, read for a different line.

findings.finding: Besi Q3 2026 orders were EUR 342.6m (+96% y/y), reported as about 15% above analyst expectations, and FY26 revenue and orders are expected above EUR 1B on AI advanced-packaging demand.
findings.link: TCB and advanced-packaging bonding overlap; Besi is far smaller in wire bond. The link is AI advanced packaging only (about $100m+ of K&S FY26 revenue).
findings.why_not_priced: Hybrid-bonding-led and mostly not K&S's product set. Small read-across to the TCB target.

findings.finding: Cohu (back-end test) reported Q3 2026 bookings +126% y/y, guided Q4 to $178m (+46% y/y) and gave a first 2027 framework of +30-40% growth, saying output builds through 2027.
findings.link: Same back-end OSAT customer base (assembly and test capex move together); different product (test handlers, not bonders).
findings.why_not_priced: A US peer reporting after K&S last spoke. It is a general back-end utilization read (test-cell utilization 82%), not bonder-specific.

findings.finding: The sector is in a sharp risk-off move. The PHLX SOX fell 12.25% on 2026-11-05 (its second-worst day on record) on AI-capex doubts after the midterms and China competition, and on 2026-10-12 KLIC fell with chip names on CXMT DRAM progress. A good print lands into a tape that has been selling semis on news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-03-03 KLIC fell 5.7% with a sector selloff. The Aug 2026 print came during a SOX drawdown of up to 29% and was sold at -3.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: The level is priced. What is unpriced is that sector beta on 11-19 can swamp the company-specific reaction either way; Nvidia's report timing around this window was not confirmed.

findings.finding: Front-expiry 25-delta skew is +19.31 vol points (downside paid) with ATM IV of 151.6% and a 9.76% event move. Open-interest put/call is 0.25, so the open positions lean to calls while new premium is paid for puts.
findings.source_date: 2026-11-18 (sealed in the baseline at 18:13 UTC from Yahoo options v7, expiry 2026-11-20)
findings.why_not_priced: Skew is the market's own directional statement and is priced by definition. Filed as the thing to beat. The ATM spread is 53% of mid, so the skew is noisy on 1,192 contracts of open interest.

findings.finding: The last print was a beat-and-raise that was sold: Q3 EPS $1.20 against about $1.06 (+$0.14) and a Q4 revenue guide of $375m against a $328.8m street figure (+14%), yet the stock moved -3.39%. The holders do not automatically pay for a beat and a high guide.
findings.why_not_priced: History, not new information. Filed because it sets the reaction function: in August the stock was coming off a $135 high, and now it comes into the print 50% below it.

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call and first guide under CEO Raj Talluri (appointed in August 2026, effective 2026-09-01, from Enovix). A new CEO's first guide carries reset risk: a conservative December-quarter range, a new investment or opex plan, or no FY27 frame.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior call under this CEO. Lester Wong, the interim CEO and CFO, gave the guides that moved the stock +19.27% and -3.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: An inference from the first-call pattern, not a document. Earnings Whispers still describes the CEO search as unresolved, so at least one preview has missed the transition entirely.
findings.independence: https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/08/kulicke-and-soffa-industries-inc-appoints-dr-raj-talluri-as-president-and-ceo/ (same release). The tone of his 2026-10-18 interview was constructive, which is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: BIS published a rule on 2026-11-09 extending the suspension of the Affiliates (50%) Rule to 2027-01-10, so the rule did not take effect on 2026-11-10. This removes a near-term risk to sales to entity-list affiliates in China, which is about 57% of K&S revenue by customer headquarters.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a non-event. Mainstream wire bonders are largely not controlled items, so the transmission is small. It does remove an excuse for a cautious China comment.

findings.finding: $226.4m of buyback authorization remained at 2026-07-04, but only $0.5m was repurchased in Q3. With the stock 50% off its high, capacity for an accelerated repurchase is there; none has been announced.
findings.why_not_priced: Optionality only. No sign of a step-up.

findings.finding: Hanmi Semiconductor is reported to have entered a Taiwanese foundry's 2.5D advanced-packaging volume line (SEMICON Taiwan, September 2026). This adds competition in the advanced-packaging bonding segment K&S targets for $150-200m of FY27 TCB revenue.
findings.link: Same segment (2.5D/TCB bonders) and the same customer class (foundry advanced packaging). The report is unconfirmed ('傳') and does not name TCB specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Taiwanese-language trade report. It matters only if the FY27 TCB target is cut on the call.

findings.finding: Summit Street Capital disclosed a complete exit from its KLIC position (about $10m) in Q3 2026, in a filing dated 2026-11-14.
findings.why_not_priced: A stale Q3 13F from one small holder; nearly worthless as a signal.

findings.finding: The whisper EPS is $1.61 against $1.44 consensus and above the $1.56 top of the guide. Buy-side expectations sit above the published bar, so an in-line or modest beat on EPS may not satisfy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 beat by $0.14 and the stock fell 3.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: A whisper is a buy-side bar. The 50% drawdown suggests the price is not anchored on it, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: https://finviz.com/news/421185/kulicke-and-soffas-whisper-tops-guidance-as-battered-stock-tests-the-fy27-upturn-story (same article, syndicated). It shares a document with the first finding, which uses the drawdown part of this source.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive against a +19 vol-point put skew and a -18.7% 20-day run, the same way the run-down argues. The skew may be pricing sector beta (SOX -12% on 11-05) and new-CEO guide risk rather than company information. p_up is held at 55, not higher, because the skew, the flat peer guides and the sold August beat argue the other way.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 / rule 6 (a reported-quarter fact inside the guided range on a name whose last beat was sold): DIGITIMES record wire-bond shipments cut from +0.6 to +0.4. Sum goes from 1.9 to 1.7.

Rule 7 (sign against a strong skew): the positive lean is kept because the skew plausibly reflects sector beta and new-CEO guide risk, not company information, and short interest is modest (4.2%, 3.7 days). p_up lowered from 57 to 55, so the scaled move goes from +1.4 to +1.0.
Rule 5 (proxies): counterparty capex and peer bookings items were already sized small as proxies. No further change.
Rule 6 (bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two roughly agreeing estimates, so no cap. No finding resolves outside the window. The 21 findings are the same set in draft and final.
